summary: Arvin hunches over a scarred metal workbench inside a hollowed-out petroleum tanker, his fingers tracing the jagged fissure of a salvaged combustion chamber. The desert sun pierces through bullet holes in the rusted metal skin, casting sharp needles of light across his weathered face as Milo approaches with a heavy roll of lead solder. Milo drops the heavy spool onto the table, the thud echoing through the cramped, oil-slicked cabin while he wipes black grease onto his stained canvas apron. Arvin stares at the hairline fracture in the steel, his jaw tightening as he calculates the atmospheric pressure that will eventually tear this recycled junk apart during the ascent. Milo leans in close, his eyes reflecting the blue flicker of a pilot light as he waits for the verdict on their only functioning engine core. "If this seam doesn't hold for sixty seconds, we aren't just losing a satellite, we're losing the whole fleet."
settingText: Nomadic fleet of rusted tankers in a salt flat basin.

dialogueInline.text: This turbine won't take the pressure of the kerosene mix, Milo.
If it doesn't fit, we make the world change shape around it.
I found a way to bypass the Aegis encryption on the primary booster.
The higher we send this thing, the harder Cyrus will hit us.

summary: Arvin stands atop a shifting white sand dune, shielding his eyes from the blinding Mojave glare as he inspects a tripod-mounted solar array. Lucia walks up the steep slope, her boots sinking deep into the fine powder, carrying a heavy encrypted data-pad that glints with corporate-grade glass. She stands inches from him, her posture rigid and predatory, as she points toward the Aegis orbital grid visible even in the daylight as faint silver streaks against the blue sky. Arvin keeps his gaze fixed on the horizon, refusing to look at the tactical overlays she attempts to slide into his field of vision, his hands clenched tightly at his sides to hide a tremor of exhaustion. Lucia shifts her weight, her shadow stretching long and dark across the pristine sand as she waits for him to acknowledge her plan for sabotage. "You see a beacon for the forgotten, but I see a target that can finally bring their grid screaming back to earth."
settingText: Inside the main mobile tanker workshop, surrounded by hanging copper wires and stacks of rusted heat shields.

dialogueInline.text: If this valve sticks by even a fraction of a millimeter, the pressure will turn us into a crater.
That junk you're building won't hit the orbit we need unless you stop pretending we're just hobbyists.
She’s got a heartbeat now, Arvin; you just have to listen to the way the metal groans.
Every launch they attempt is another signature on their own death warrant, and I am the clerk.

summary: Cyrus stands at the jagged edge of a massive limestone quarry, his polished black armor reflecting the harsh overhead sun while he stares down at a discarded rocket strut. Beside him, a nervous Aegis technician kneels in the dirt, operating a haptic controller that directs a swarm of low-altitude surveillance drones hovering over the deep excavation site. Cyrus picks up the rusted strut, turning it over in his gloved hands, his eyes narrowing as he identifies the crude, hand-etched serial number Arvin carved into the metal. He tosses the heavy part back into the dust and steps toward the technician, his massive frame looming over the flickering holographic displays of the drone feed. Cyrus grips the technician's shoulder, his fingers pressing into the fabric of the uniform as he stares at the heat signatures appearing on the screen. "Scour every cave within ten miles; I want to smell the kerosene before the sun sets."
settingText: The interior of the rusted Nomad Tanker, cluttered with brass fittings and copper coils.

dialogueInline.text: If this seam parts by even a fraction during ignition, the entire manifold becomes a pipe bomb.
It’ll hold for ten seconds, which is nine more than we actually need to clear the atmosphere.
The wind is shifting toward the Aegis towers, so we should consider a steeper launch trajectory.
They are building toys out of garbage, but even a toy can cause a fire in my sky.
